category.name: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws

rule.name: Untrusted Data in 'document.getElementById().value'
rule.rule_desc: The code accepts or reads externally influenced data. Trace it to security-sensitive operations and identify the validation and authorization required by each destination.
rule.vuln_desc: External input may cause injection, incorrect decisions, or unauthorized data access if it reaches a sensitive operation without the controls required by that operation. Reading input alone does not establish a vulnerability.
rule.developer: Validate type, size, and allowed values at trust boundaries, and apply destination-specific parameter binding or output encoding. Enforce authorization independently of input validation.
rule.reviewer: Ensure that proper input handling is in place for user input obtained through `document. getElementById(). value`. Verify that developers have implemented appropriate input validation and sanitization techniques to prevent security vulnerabilities related to unvalidated input. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Untrusted Data in InnerHTML
rule.rule_desc: Application data is inserted into an HTML or script rendering context, or marked safe in a way that may bypass automatic encoding.
rule.vuln_desc: If attacker-controlled content reaches an executable browser context, it may run under the application’s origin, read accessible session data, or perform actions with the victim’s permissions.
rule.developer: Use automatic context-aware output encoding and data-only DOM APIs. Sanitize deliberately accepted rich HTML with a maintained allowlist sanitizer and avoid marking untrusted content as safe.
rule.reviewer: Potentially untrusted data is assigned to the innerHTML property. Assess whether the code implements proper input validation and output encoding techniques to prevent XSS vulnerabilities when updating element content. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Untrusted Data in 'document.write'
rule.rule_desc: Application data is inserted into an HTML or script rendering context, or marked safe in a way that may bypass automatic encoding.
rule.vuln_desc: If attacker-controlled content reaches an executable browser context, it may run under the application’s origin, read accessible session data, or perform actions with the victim’s permissions.
rule.developer: Use automatic context-aware output encoding and data-only DOM APIs. Sanitize deliberately accepted rich HTML with a maintained allowlist sanitizer and avoid marking untrusted content as safe.
rule.reviewer: The code uses `document. write()` or assigns potentially untrusted values to the `innerHTML` property. Assess whether proper input validation and output encoding techniques are implemented to prevent DOM-based cross-site scripting vulnerabilities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Handlebars Unescaped String
rule.description: Detects unescaped Handlebars strings in code.
rule.rule_desc: Application data is inserted into an HTML or script rendering context, or marked safe in a way that may bypass automatic encoding.
rule.vuln_desc: If attacker-controlled content reaches an executable browser context, it may run under the application’s origin, read accessible session data, or perform actions with the victim’s permissions.
rule.developer: Use automatic context-aware output encoding and data-only DOM APIs. Sanitize deliberately accepted rich HTML with a maintained allowlist sanitizer and avoid marking untrusted content as safe.
rule.reviewer: Verify that proper input sanitization techniques are applied when using Handlebars strings. Ensure that developers use Handlebars' built-in escaping mechanisms or equivalent custom sanitization methods to mitigate the risk of XSS vulnerabilities. Also assess the implementation of output encoding and confirm that user input is properly sanitized before rendering it in the application. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure Method Call: child_process.exec()
rule.rule_desc: The code invokes a process or shell execution API. Trace the executable, arguments, shell use, and source of externally supplied values.
rule.vuln_desc: If attacker-controlled data changes command syntax or executable selection, an attacker may execute commands with application privileges, read or modify files, or disrupt service.
rule.developer: Use a fixed executable with a separate argument array and avoid a shell where possible. Validate arguments for the selected program and allowlist permitted operations.
rule.reviewer: Verify whether the code implements sufficient measures to prevent remote OS command execution vulnerabilities. Check whether the usage of `child_process. exec()` is necessary, and if so, ensure that proper input validation, sanitization, and command parameterization techniques are implemented to prevent command injection attacks. Also assess the context in which this function is used and verify that security best practices are followed to mitigate any potential risks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure Method Call: eval|setTimeout|setInterval
rule.rule_desc: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
rule.vuln_desc: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
rule.developer: Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.
rule.reviewer: Verify whether the code uses the `eval`, `setTimeout`, or `setInterval` functions. Assess whether the usage is justified and if proper input validation and sanitization techniques are implemented to prevent code injection vulnerabilities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Weak Cryptography
rule.rule_desc: The checked source uses a random generator, cryptographic primitive, or initialization value whose suitability depends on its security purpose and inputs.
rule.vuln_desc: Predictable secrets or unsuitable cryptographic parameters may enable credential guessing, reveal plaintext, or weaken integrity when used to protect security-sensitive data. Non-security hashes and identifiers do not establish this condition.
rule.developer: Use a cryptographically secure generator for secrets and modern purpose-appropriate cryptography. Use unique nonces, protected keys, and a vetted password-hashing scheme where passwords are stored.
rule.reviewer: Weak cryptographic functions are used in the code. Assess whether the code uses secure cryptographic algorithms and if best practices for encryption and hashing are followed. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Weak Random Number Generation
rule.rule_desc: The checked source uses a random generator, cryptographic primitive, or initialization value whose suitability depends on its security purpose and inputs.
rule.vuln_desc: Predictable secrets or unsuitable cryptographic parameters may enable credential guessing, reveal plaintext, or weaken integrity when used to protect security-sensitive data. Non-security hashes and identifiers do not establish this condition.
rule.developer: Use a cryptographically secure generator for secrets and modern purpose-appropriate cryptography. Use unique nonces, protected keys, and a vetted password-hashing scheme where passwords are stored.
rule.reviewer: Verify that Math.random() is not used where cryptographic randomness is required. Confirm that security-sensitive identifiers use a CSPRNG. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Routes
rule.rule_desc: The code declares an entry point, model, destination, or configuration value that may cross a trust boundary. Identify callers, recipients, and the required data-access policy.
rule.vuln_desc: A boundary that trusts unauthorized callers or exposes private output may permit data disclosure or state changes. A declaration, address, or architectural marker alone does not establish such a failure.
rule.developer: Trace the actual boundary, restrict accepted inputs and recipients, and enforce authentication and object-level authorization where required. Verify both authorized and denied use cases.
rule.reviewer: Verify whether the code contains hardcoded routes and assess the potential security implications. Ensure that sensitive information, such as internal URLs, API endpoints, or authentication routes, is not exposed through hardcoded routes. Also check if the code implements appropriate access control measures and adheres to secure coding practices, such as using configuration files or dynamic routing mechanisms. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Stack Trace or Error Disclosure (Node/Express)
rule.rule_desc: The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output.
rule.vuln_desc: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
rule.developer: Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration.
rule.reviewer: Confirm that HTTP responses never include raw error objects, stack traces, or internal diagnostic details. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Node Inspector Exposed via --inspect
rule.rule_desc: A configuration or API enables development diagnostics, process inspection, or debugging. Verify whether it applies to a deployed production artifact.
rule.vuln_desc: An actor with access to an enabled debugging interface may inspect private state or influence application execution; exposed development endpoints may disclose internal implementation details.
rule.developer: Disable debugging and development endpoints in production, bind necessary diagnostic services to restricted interfaces, and verify the final deployed artifact and access policy.
rule.reviewer: Verify runtime scripts and deployment manifests do not expose inspector endpoints in production environments. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Insecure HTTP Parser Enabled
rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
rule.vuln_desc: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
rule.developer: Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.
rule.reviewer: Confirm parser hardening remains enabled across app servers and reverse-proxy boundaries. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Weak Mitigation: Using disable|bypass|ignore|suppress|unsafe
rule.rule_desc: The code contains a security-control marker. Its presence is a review surface rather than evidence that the control is defective or consistently enforced.
rule.vuln_desc: No adverse security consequence follows from the presence of a protection alone. If it is bypassed or applied outside the correct context, the protected operation may still permit injection or unauthorized access.
rule.developer: Verify that the control applies to every relevant entry point and uses the required context and policy. Retain effective protections; test bypass cases before recommending a change.
rule.reviewer: Identify weak or inadequate security mitigations in the code and recommend implementing stronger security measures. Assess whether the application applies appropriate security controls and avoids relying on weak mitigations that may be easily bypassed by attackers. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: SQL Query: SELECT Statements with WHERE or ORDER BY
rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
rule.vuln_desc: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
rule.developer: Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.
rule.reviewer: Check if parameterized queries or query bindings are used with SELECT statements containing WHERE or ORDER BY clauses in JavaScript applications to ensure secure handling of user input. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
rule.vuln_desc: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
rule.developer: Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.
rule.reviewer: Verify that SQL queries in JavaScript applications select only the required columns to minimize data exposure risks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.reviewer: Inspect any INSERT statements to confirm secure parameterization in JavaScript applications and ensure that user input is handled safely to minimize injection risks. rule.rule_desc: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.

rule.developer: Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.

rule.name: Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR)
rule.rule_desc: The checked code implements an identity, access-control, or abuse-prevention decision. Determine the trusted verifier, protected resources, and whether the control is enforced on every relevant path.
rule.vuln_desc: If identity or resource authorization can be bypassed, an attacker may impersonate a user, access another user’s data, or perform restricted operations. A control’s presence alone does not establish a weakness.
rule.developer: Enforce authentication and object-level authorization on the trusted server or privileged boundary. Use strong verifier material, appropriate rate limits and recovery controls, and test access by unauthenticated and insufficiently privileged callers.
rule.reviewer: Verify whether the code implements proper authorization and access control mechanisms to prevent IDOR vulnerabilities. Check whether user input used to access resources is properly validated, sanitized, and authorized. Reviewers should assess the effectiveness of the implemented measures in mitigating IDOR risks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
rule.rule_desc: The application makes an outbound request whose destination may be influenced by external data. Resolve URL construction, redirects, DNS results, and network reachability.
rule.vuln_desc: If an attacker can select a reachable destination, the application may expose internal services or metadata credentials, or send protected data to an unauthorized recipient.
rule.developer: Allowlist required destinations and protocols, validate resolved addresses and every redirect, and restrict outbound access to internal and metadata services.
rule.reviewer: XMLHttpRequest, fetch, axios, http. request, https. request, http. get, https. get, http. post, https. post, http. put, https. put, http. delete, https. delete, or $. ajax functions are used with potentially untrusted URLs. Assess whether proper input validation and URL restriction mechanisms are implemented to mitigate SSRF vulnerabilities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Prototype Pollution
rule.rule_desc: The code writes object properties or merges data in a way that may affect prototype state. Determine whether externally supplied keys can reach the operation.
rule.vuln_desc: An attacker who changes shared prototype properties may alter authorization decisions or other application behavior; some reachable gadgets may also lead to data disclosure or code execution.
rule.developer: Reject prototype-manipulating keys such as __proto__, constructor, and prototype where appropriate. Use safe own-property handling, null-prototype dictionaries, and maintained merge libraries.
rule.reviewer: The code directly uses or modifies the `__proto__` property or assigns values to properties of `Object. prototype` (excluding `hasOwnProperty`). Assess whether proper precautions are taken to prevent prototype pollution vulnerabilities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Missing Cookie Security Flags
rule.rule_desc: The code handles session state or configures cookies and session secrets. Resolve cookie attributes, token generation, lifetime, and server-side validation.
rule.vuln_desc: Weak session secrets, exposed cookies, or inadequate expiry may allow session theft, token forgery, or continued access after the user’s intended authorization ends.
rule.developer: Use strong unpredictable session secrets, rotate tokens on privilege changes, and enforce expiry and revocation. Set Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite attributes for sensitive browser cookies.
rule.reviewer: Confirm that all cookies setting session or authentication state include httpOnly, secure, and sameSite attributes. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
